title: Sensitivity labels: what they classify, protect and tell Copilot to leave alone
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports its controls, licensing statements and operational limits. It reports the disagreements between Microsoft's licensing and container-label guidance rather than silently choosing one account.

claims.claim: The classic label-creation route is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > + Create a label.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels
On the Sensitivity labels page, select + Create a label to start the new sensitivity label configuration.

claims.claim: New-Label -Name <label name> -DisplayName <display name> -Tooltip <tooltip> creates a sensitivity label.
claims.quote:
Use the New-Label cmdlet to create sensitivity labels in your organization.
New-Label
    [-Name] <String>
    -DisplayName <String>
    -Tooltip <String>

claims.claim: New-Label and New-LabelPolicy are Security & Compliance PowerShell operations.
claims.quote: You can now use Security & Compliance PowerShell to create and configure all the settings you see in your labeling admin center.

claims.claim: The modern label scheme uses + Create followed by Label.
claims.quote: On the Sensitivity labels page, select + Create and then Label to start the new sensitivity label configuration.

claims.claim: Set-Label changes an existing label.
claims.quote:
you can now fully script the creation and maintenance of sensitivity labels and sensitivity label policies.
See the following documentation for supported parameters and values:
New-Label
New-LabelPolicy
Set-Label
Set-LabelPolicy

claims.claim: Label policies are created through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies.
On the Label policies page, select Publish label to start the Create policy configuration.

claims.claim: New-LabelPolicy -Name <policy name> -Labels <label names> creates a policy containing the named labels.
claims.quote:
New-LabelPolicy -Name "Research and Development" -Labels "R and D","R and D Management"
This example creates the sensitivity label policy named Research and Development that contains sensitivity labels named R and D and R and D Management.

claims.claim: New-LabelPolicy has a location parameter named ExchangeLocation.
claims.quote: The ExchangeLocation parameter specifies the mailboxes to include in the policy. A valid value is a mailbox.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy changes a published label policy.
claims.quote: Additional label policy settings are available with the Set-LabelPolicy cmdlet from Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive label support is enabled through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Turn on now.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels.
If you see a message to turn on the ability to process content in Office online files, select Turn on now:

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true enables SharePoint and OneDrive sensitivity-label support.
claims.quote:
To enable the new capabilities, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableAIPIntegration parameter:
Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true

claims.claim: Enabling SharePoint and OneDrive label support through the portal requires a global administrator.
claims.quote: You must sign in as a global administrator for your tenant.

claims.claim: Multi-Geo tenants must enable the support with PowerShell separately for every geo-location.
claims.quote:
If you have Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, you must use PowerShell to enable this support for all your geo-locations.
For Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo: Repeat steps 1 and 2 for each of your remaining geo-locations.

claims.claim: OneNote label support requires an additional Set-SPOTenant parameter.
claims.quote:
If you want to additionally enable sensitivity labels for OneNote (supported at the section level), run Set-SPOTenant again, but use the following command:
Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelforOneNote $true

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a portal switch for enabling tenant-level sensitivity-label support for groups, teams and sites.
claims.quote: Searched: enable sensitivity labels containers EnableMIPLabels admin portal UI enable groups sites PowerShell. Opened Entra Assign sensitivity labels to Microsoft 365 groups and Purview Use sensitivity labels to protect collaborative workspaces; no enablement UI documented.

claims.claim: Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId <setting id> -BodyParameter <params> enables the directory setting used for container labels.
EnableMIPLabels must be True for Microsoft 365 group labels.
claims.quote: The feature is enabled and EnableMIPLabels is set to True in the Microsoft Graph PowerShell module.

claims.claim: Execute-AzureAdLabelSync in Security & Compliance PowerShell synchronises labels to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Labels are synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID with the Execute-AzureAdLabelSync cmdlet in the Security & Compliance PowerShell module.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Cost and licensing: Groups and sites
claims.claim: Configuring Microsoft 365 group labels requires at least one active Microsoft Entra ID P1 licence in the organisation.
claims.quote: To configure this feature, there must be at least one active Microsoft Entra ID P1 license in your Microsoft Entra organization.

claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling policies are created through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > + Create auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies.
Select + Create auto-labeling policy.

claims.claim: New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy with Name, SharePointLocation, ApplySensitivityLabel and Mode TestWithoutNotifications creates an auto-labeling policy for the selected SharePoint site.
claims.quote: New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Name <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -SharePointLocation "<SharePointSiteLocation>" -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications

claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling needs an entitlement listed for Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling, not just a client-only entitlement.
claims.quote: Check the Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling entry in the feature matrix linked below. Client-only entitlements don't establish service-side entitlement.

claims.claim: The Copilot DLP route is Purview > Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork > rule > Content contains > Sensitivity labels.
claims.quote:
Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.
Select the Custom template, then Custom policy.
On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
Content contains > Sensitivity labels

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <rule name> -Policy <policy name> -AdvancedRule <advanced rule> -RestrictAccess <settings> creates the label-based Copilot content-processing rule.
claims.quote: New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The label-based DLP rule action is Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content.
claims.quote: Content contains > Sensitivity labels | Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content

claims.claim: The Copilot rule example sets RestrictAccess to ExcludeContentProcessing = Block.
claims.quote: -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The policy holding the example Copilot rule uses EnforcementPlanes CopilotExperiences.
claims.quote: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences")

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels are Microsoft Purview Information Protection classifications that can protect content.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels from Microsoft Purview Information Protection let you classify and protect your organization's data

claims.claim: Labels can encrypt files and emails.
claims.quote: Control access to content by using encryption for emails, meeting invites, and documents to prevent unauthorized people from accessing this data.

claims.claim: Labels can configure privacy and sharing for sites and groups.
claims.quote: These settings include privacy settings, external user access and external sharing, access from unmanaged devices, private teams discoverability, and sharing controls for channels.

claims.claim: Labels can enforce content markings.
claims.quote: Mark the content when you use Office apps, by adding watermarks, headers, or footers to email, meeting invites, or documents that have the label applied.

claims.claim: Labels are stored in file and email metadata.
claims.quote: Because the label is stored in clear text in the metadata for files and emails, third-party apps and services can read it

claims.claim: A file or email label stays with the content wherever it is saved.
claims.quote: Because the label is stored in metadata for files and emails, the label stays with the content, no matter where you save or store it.

claims.claim: Administrators create labels and publish them in label policies.
claims.quote: Publish the labels. After your sensitivity labels are configured, publish them by using a label policy.

claims.claim: Users can apply labels manually.
claims.quote: Then, end users apply labels to emails and documents.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling can apply labels.
claims.quote: When you create a sensitivity label, you can automatically assign that label to Microsoft 365 items such as files and emails when the data matches conditions that you specify.

claims.claim: Office, SharePoint and other supporting services enforce label settings.
claims.quote: Finally, Office or third-party apps/services enforce protection based on the applied labels.

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism
claims.claim: Label scope determines which label settings are available and where the label is available.
claims.quote:
The scope determines two things:
Which label settings you can configure for that label
The availability of the label to apps and services, which includes whether users can see and select the label

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism
claims.claim: Files and other data assets are a sensitivity-label scope.
claims.quote: By default, the Files & other data assets scope is always selected for a new label.

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism
claims.claim: Emails are a sensitivity-label scope.
claims.quote: Typically, you select the Emails scope together with Files & other data assets

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism
claims.claim: Meetings are a sensitivity-label scope.
claims.quote: The scope for Meetings includes calendar events, Teams meetings options, and Team chat.

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism
claims.claim: Groups and sites are a sensitivity-label scope.
claims.quote: The Groups & sites scope becomes available and selected by default when you enable sensitivity labels for containers and synchronize labels.

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism; Risks and limits: Container labels
claims.claim: A container label protects the container but does not label the items in it.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels and therefore don't apply any item-level label settings, such as content markings and encryption.

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism
claims.claim: Label priority is determined by the order of the label list.
claims.quote: In this list, the order of the labels is important because it sets their priority.

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends placing the most restrictive label at the bottom of the list.
claims.quote: You want your most restrictive sensitivity label, such as Highly Confidential, to appear at the bottom of the list, and your least restrictive sensitivity label, such as Personal or Public, to appear at the top.

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism
claims.claim: An item supports one sensitivity label from an organisation.
claims.quote: Each item that supports sensitivity labels can have a single sensitivity label applied to it from your organization.

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism; controls[1]
claims.claim: Label policies determine which users and groups see which labels.
claims.quote: Choose which users and groups see the labels. Labels can be published to include or exclude specific users and supported groups.

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism
claims.claim: Label policies can specify a default label.
claims.quote: Specify a default label for unlabeled documents and Loop components and pages, emails and meeting invites, new containers

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism
claims.claim: Label policies can require justification for lowering a label.
claims.quote: For files, emails, and meetings, but not for groups and sites (used by Teams and SharePoint), if a user tries to remove a label or replace it with a label that has a lower priority, by default the user must provide a justification

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism
claims.claim: Label policies can require mandatory labelling.
claims.quote: Require users to apply a label for the different types of items and the containers that support sensitivity labels. Also known as mandatory labeling

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism
claims.claim: Client-side auto-labeling in Office apps supports applying or recommending a label.
claims.quote: This method supports recommending a label to users, as well as automatically applying a label.

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism; controls[4]
claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling policies apply to saved SharePoint and OneDrive content and email processed by Exchange Online.
claims.quote: Service-side labeling when content is already saved (in SharePoint or OneDrive) or emailed (processed by Exchange Online): Use an auto-labeling policy.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot recognises sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, and Copilot agents recognize and use the sensitivity labels that you apply to protect your organization's data.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Copilot Chat recognises sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, and Copilot agents recognize and use the sensitivity labels that you apply to protect your organization's data.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Copilot agents recognise sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, and Copilot agents recognize and use the sensitivity labels that you apply to protect your organization's data.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Copilot Chat displays the highest-priority sensitivity label from the data used.
claims.quote: in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat conversations that can reference data from different types of items, users see the sensitivity label with the highest priority

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels; Why it matters; summary
claims.claim: For label-encrypted items, Copilot and agents require the user's EXTRACT right to return content, subject to the stated Edge exception.
claims.quote: If the labels apply encryption from Microsoft Purview Information Protection, Copilot and agents check the usage rights for the user. Then, Copilot and agents return data from an item only if the user is granted permissions to copy (the EXTRACT usage right) from that item.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: EXTRACT is permission to copy content.
claims.quote: The usage right that grants permission to copy text is EXTRACT, with the more user-friendly, common name of Copy.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Without DLP in Edge, Copilot in Edge and Windows can reference encrypted content in the active Edge tab without EXTRACT.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Edge, Microsoft 365 Copilot in Windows: Unless data loss prevention (DLP) is used in Edge, Copilot can reference encrypted content from the active browser tab in Edge when that content doesn't grant the user EXTRACT usage rights.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Copilot in Word supports source-label inheritance for newly created content.
claims.quote: If you use Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook to create new content based on an item that has a sensitivity label applied, the sensitivity label from the source file is automatically inherited, with the label's protection settings.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint supports source-label inheritance for newly created content.
claims.quote: Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook support sensitivity label inheritance for newly created content.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Copilot in Outlook supports source-label inheritance for newly created content.
claims.quote: Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook support sensitivity label inheritance for newly created content.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Label inheritance is not supported when source encryption uses user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: If a user asks Copilot or agents to create new content from labeled and encrypted items, label inheritance isn't supported when the encryption is configured for user-defined permissions or if the encryption was applied independently from the label.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: When source-label inheritance cannot be supported for user-defined encryption, the user cannot send the data to the destination item.
claims.quote: The user won't be able to send this data to the destination item.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Retention is the separate mechanism for keeping or deleting content.
claims.quote: Although the main purpose of retention labels is to retain or delete content, you can also use retention labels without turning on any retention or other actions.

claims.claim: Purview DLP policies can exclude files and emails from Copilot processing based on their sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: create DLP policies that use the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location with the Content contains > Sensitivity labels condition to exclude items from being processed.

claims.claim: eDiscovery search conditions can use sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: The condition builder to create search queries in eDiscovery supports sensitivity labels that are applied to content.

claims.claim: The service description says Information Protection features are enabled at tenant level for all users by default.
claims.quote: By default, Information Protection features are enabled at the tenant level for all users within the tenant.

claims.claim: Several per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Why it matters
claims.claim: User licensing requirements depend on the sensitivity-label features used.
claims.quote: the licensing requirements for users depend on the features you use.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Administrators need an appropriate licence to manage sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Admins also need a license to manage sensitivity labels.

Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/FLW

Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW

claims.claim: Applying labels in Data Map and using protection policies for non-Microsoft 365 sources requires pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Specific to non-Microsoft 365 data sources, applying sensitivity labels in the Data Map and using protection policies requires you to set up pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: Data Map sensitivity-label capabilities are documented as preview.
claims.quote: Extend sensitivity labels to assets in Microsoft Purview Data Map: When you turn on this capability, currently in preview

claims.claim: Protection policies are documented as preview.
claims.quote: Protection policies are currently in preview and apply to items stored outside Microsoft 365.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Labels not enabled
claims.claim: Before label support is enabled, SharePoint and OneDrive cannot process label-encrypted files for coauthoring, eDiscovery, DLP and search.
claims.quote: Until you enable this feature, these services can't process encrypted files, which means that coauthoring, eDiscovery, data loss prevention, search, and other collaborative features won't work for these files.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: An auto-labeling policy automatically created from label configuration runs in simulation mode when saved.
claims.quote: By default, all locations for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange are included in the auto-label policy, and when the policy is saved, it runs in simulation mode.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: That automatic policy creation does not check whether SharePoint and OneDrive label support is enabled.
claims.quote: There's no check that you've enabled sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive, which is one of the prerequisites for auto-labeling to apply to content in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check; What to check
claims.claim: Enabled SharePoint and OneDrive label support is a prerequisite for auto-labeling content in those services.
claims.quote: enabled sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive, which is one of the prerequisites for auto-labeling to apply to content in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: Auto-labeling has a throughput ceiling of 500,000 files per day.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies. This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate; actual throughput can be lower.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: The auto-labeling policy limit is 100 policies per tenant.
claims.quote: Maximum of 100 auto-labeling policies per tenant.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: A policy configured in the portal can explicitly select up to 1,000 SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: In the portal, each policy can target up to 1,000 explicitly included or excluded SharePoint sites

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: An auto-labeling policy simulation supports up to 20,000,000 matched files.
claims.quote: Simulation mode supports up to 20,000,000 matched files. If more than this number of files are matched from an auto-labeling policy, you can't turn on the policy to apply the labels.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: The overview says deleting a label does not automatically remove the label or protection from content.
claims.quote: If you delete a sensitivity label from the Microsoft Purview portal, the label isn't automatically removed from content, and any protection settings continue to be enforced on content that had that label applied.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: The detailed deletion guide says container labels are removed and their configured settings cease to be enforced.
claims.quote: For containers, such as sites in SharePoint and Teams: The label is removed and any settings that were configured with that label are no longer enforced.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: Deleting an encrypting label can remove encryption from processable documents in enabled SharePoint and OneDrive services.
claims.quote: If the deleted label applied encryption and the services can process the encrypted contents, the encryption is removed. Egress actions from these services result in the same outcome.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: Deleting an encrypting label archives its protection template and prevents reusing the label name.
claims.quote: If the label applied encryption, the underlying protection template is archived so that previously protected content can still be opened. Because of this archived protection template, you can't create a new label with the same name.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An encrypting default label
claims.claim: Microsoft discourages an encrypting default document label because external recipients may lack suitable apps or authorisable accounts.
claims.quote: It's usually not a good idea to select a label that applies encryption as a default label to documents. For example, many organizations need to send and share documents with external users who might not have apps that support the encryption or they might not use an account that can be authorized.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A policy scope is not an access list
claims.claim: Azure Rights Management does not support non-email-enabled security groups or exclusions for protection, so publishing policy scope need not determine protected-content access.
claims.quote: For labels that apply protection, Azure Rights Management doesn't support non-email-enabled security groups or exclusions, so the publishing policy scope doesn't necessarily determine who can access protected content.

claims.claim: A site owner can change external sharing options by applying or changing the site's label.
claims.quote: When you configure and publish the label settings for external sharing options and the authentication context, a site owner can now set and change these options for a site by applying or changing the sensitivity label for a team or site.

claims.claim: The Entra guide says published group-setting changes are not automatically applied to already-labelled groups.
claims.quote: When you make changes to group settings for a published label in the Microsoft Purview portal, those policy changes aren't automatically applied on the labeled groups.

claims.claim: The Purview container guide instead says to allow at least 24 hours for changed site and group settings to replicate to all labelled containers.
claims.quote: As a best practice, don't change the site and group settings for a sensitivity label after the label has been applied to teams, groups, or sites. If you do, remember to wait at least 24 hours for the changes to replicate to all containers that have the label applied.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes take time
claims.claim: Microsoft advises allowing 24 hours for label and label-policy changes.
claims.quote: For labels and label policy settings, allow 24 hours for the changes to propagate through the services.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes take time
claims.claim: Changes dependent on group membership can take 24 to 48 hours.
claims.quote: for configurations that depend on populating a new group and group membership changes, or network replication latency and bandwidth restrictions, these changes might take 24-48 hours.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot DLP gaps
claims.claim: DLP cannot scan file contents uploaded directly into Copilot prompts.
claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot DLP gaps; What to check
claims.claim: Word, Excel and PowerPoint evaluate Copilot DLP at file open, so a mid-session label applies on the next open.
claims.quote: In Word, Excel, and PowerPoint the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy to prevent Copilot from processing content is evaluated at file open. If a sensitivity label is applied mid-session, the policy will be enforced starting the next time the file is opened.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot DLP gaps
claims.claim: Copilot label-based DLP covers emails sent on or after 1 January 2025.
claims.quote: Emails sent on or after January 1, 2025.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot DLP gaps
claims.claim: Copilot label-based DLP does not support calendar invites.
claims.quote: Calendar invites aren't supported.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot DLP gaps
claims.claim: Items excluded from processing by sensitivity-label DLP can still appear in Copilot citations.
claims.quote: Identified items still appear in the citations of the response, but Copilot and Cowork don't access or use the content of the item in the response.

claims.claim: BlockContentAnalysisServices can exclude labelled content from Microsoft 365 Copilot in supported Office apps.
claims.quote: Although content with the configured sensitivity label will be excluded from Microsoft 365 Copilot in the named Office apps, the content remains available to Microsoft 365 Copilot for other scenarios.

claims.claim: BlockContentAnalysisServices is a label-based privacy control rather than a requirement to encrypt the labelled content.
claims.quote:
prevent all documents and emails with this label in Office apps from being sent to Microsoft connected experiences for analysis:
Set-Label -Identity "8faca7b8-8d20-48a3-8ea2-0f96310a848e" -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"}

claims.claim: The connected-experiences exclusion does not exclude the labelled content from Copilot in Teams.
claims.quote: the content remains available to Microsoft 365 Copilot for other scenarios. For example, in Teams, and in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The connected-experiences exclusion does not exclude the labelled content from Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: the content remains available to Microsoft 365 Copilot for other scenarios. For example, in Teams, and in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: A tenant supports at most 500 labels applying encryption that specifies users and permissions.
claims.quote: If the label applies encryption that specifies the users and permissions, there's a maximum of 500 labels per tenant supported with this configuration.

claims.claim: The Information Protection role groups are documented permission options for creating and managing labels in the Purview portal.
claims.quote:
You can use the following role groups:
Information Protection
Information Protection Admins
Information Protection Analysts
Information Protection Investigators
Information Protection Readers

claims.claim: A custom role group containing Sensitivity Label Administrator is an alternative for managing labels.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using the default role groups, you can create a new role group and add the Sensitivity Label Administrator role to this group.

claims.claim: Sensitivity Label Reader is the read-only custom-role option.
claims.quote: For a read-only role, use Sensitivity Label Reader.

claims.claim: Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator and Security Administrator role groups are alternative label-management permissions.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: Label-management permissions are not required merely to apply labels in apps or services.
claims.quote: These permissions are required only to create and configure sensitivity labels and their label policies. They are not required to apply the labels in apps or services.

claims.claim: Assigning a label to a Microsoft 365 group requires group ownership or at least Groups Administrator.
claims.quote: Has sufficient privileges to assign sensitivity labels. The user must be the group owner or at least a Groups Administrator.

claims.claim: Sensitivity-label activities are listed in Microsoft's Audit log activities documentation.
claims.quote: Audit sensitivity labeling in my organization | Audit log activities - Sensitivity label activities

claims.claim: Information Protection posture reports are in preview.
claims.quote: Information Protection posture reports, Data Loss Prevention posture reports, and Custom posture reports are in preview.

claims.claim: Information Protection posture reports are under Information Protection > Reports in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote:
You find Posture Reports in the Microsoft Purview portal:
Information Protection > Reports
Data Loss Prevention > Reports

claims.claim: Label-policy order determines which policy settings win when assigned policies conflict.
claims.quote: If there's a conflict in settings from multiple policies, the settings from the policy with the highest priority (highest order number) is applied. In other words, the highest priority wins for each setting.

claims.where: What to check: Turn on now banner
claims.claim: The Turn on now banner indicates that SharePoint and OneDrive label-processing support still needs enabling.
claims.quote:
If you see a message to turn on the ability to process content in Office online files, select Turn on now:
The command runs immediately and when the page is next refreshed, you no longer see the message or button.

claims.claim: The sensitivity-label DLP processing restriction also applies to Copilot Cowork.
claims.quote: This feature is available in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Cowork, and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
